title: hello-channel-discord — the same shape, a different platform (target: channel)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “Serves Discord's interactions endpoint at POST /discord/events — one model turn per slash command, button click, or modal submit.” Signed HTTP only: no Gateway WebSocket, and registering the commands is a call provision prints for you.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the credentials
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the boot beats — Anthropic plus the three Discord refs.

verify.note: operator-supplied demos/.env; the Discord beats also want DISCORD_APPLICATION_ID + DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN + DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec: swap the platform, keep the shape

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: “Same target: channel as the Slack starter. The platform is a block, not a rewrite.”

beats.label: The agent — model and instructions
beats.cue: “When a slash command, button click, or modal submit fires, reply concisely.”

beats.label: Give it one hand
beats.cue: Read only — no shell here, so there is nothing to ask about at runtime.

beats.label: Wire it to Discord
beats.cue: Three env refs: application id, bot token, and the public key that verifies each interaction.

beats.label: Route an interaction to a session
beats.cue: The same sessionKey: thread as the Slack starter — but read it in Discord's terms: “thread” is a real thread channel, and a slash command in a plain channel is keyed by its own interaction id, so each one opens a fresh session.

beats.label: State the policy anyway
beats.cue: One rule: Read is always allowed. The permission block is in the spec even when it is short.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Same IR target as the Slack starter — only the adapter and its secret refs differ.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target channel (discord adapter, three secret refs)

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN, with no token in the room.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (4 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the spec env refs gate

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: The Discord adapter is one import swap; the gateway, router and agent are the same three files.

beats.label: Find the platform in the bundle
beats.cue: “One import names the platform. Everything else the compiler emits is shape, not Discord.”

verify.note: two hits: channel-adapter-discord (the platform) and channel-adapter-base (the shape)

beats.label: Ask run to run it
beats.cue: “run is the cli/browser REPL. A daemon isn't a chat — the CLI names the shapes it takes.”

verify.note: deliberate rejection — `crewhaus run supports target: cli or browser (got "channel")`

beats.label: Boot the daemon with no secrets
beats.cue: “Scrub the secrets back out and it names every one of them — before it binds a port — then exits 2.”
beats.command: env -u DISCORD_APPLICATION_ID -u DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN -u DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY bun live/dist/daemon.ts

verify.note: designed refusal — `[daemon] missing required env vars: DISCORD_APPLICATION_ID, DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. env -u is load-bearing: Setup already sourced .env into this same terminal, so without it a provisioned take boots the daemon instead of showing the gate

beats.label: Boot it for real
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Secrets present, and it serves the interactions endpoint on PORT — 3000 by default.” Backgrounded, so the terminal stays yours.

verify.note: needs the three Discord vars + Anthropic credentials; long-running HTTP interactions endpoint — `&` keeps the manifest's one terminal free for the beats after it (`kill %1` when the take is done, or port 3000 is still held on the re-take)

beats.label: Fire a slash command
beats.cue: [manual] Invoke the command in Discord; the adapter renders it as “/<name> <options>” for the agent.

verify.note: a real Discord app + a public interactions URL has to deliver the interaction first

groups.title: One more thing · the Discord app setup is a command too

beats.label: Derive the interactions endpoint + invite URL
beats.cue: “channel provision derives the endpoint PATCH, the permission bits, and the invite URL.”
beats.command: crewhaus channel provision live/crewhaus.yaml --platform discord --base-url https://demo.example.com --dry-run

verify.note: dry run prints the applications/@me PATCH payload + invite URL + the slash-command registration step; writes nothing

beats.label: Preview the endpoint doctor
beats.cue: “Exactly one call it would make — GET applications/@me — before you own an app.”

verify.note: prints the would-GET applications/@me plan; no network

beats.label: Run the endpoint doctor for real
beats.cue: [needs-key] Live application fetch — exit 1 the moment the interactions URL doesn't match.

verify.note: hits discord.com with $DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN; exits 1 on a mismatched interactions endpoint
